title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Chopped-Up Beam
summary: Chelm's great study hall needs a strong beam, but when it reaches the gate an argument begins: do we hold it from the right or from the left? To settle it, the wise men saw the beam in half, and again, and again, until only a little pile of sawdust is left. But little Gitele knows how to carry a beam together. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
In Chelm they built a study hall, as big as a mountain, tall and grand,
and the ceiling creaked: "I'm missing a beam! Just one! A strong beam — quick, lend a hand!"
So they climbed to the forest and cut down a tree, as big and strong as could be,
and planed it and polished it into a beam — straight, without a crack to see.

Four strong men carried the beam, with Yokel singing in front, leading the way,
and there was the big gate! One more step — and inside they'd go, hooray!

When they reached the gate, the green hats shouted, "From the right! That's clear!"
And the orange hats yelled, "From the left! You don't understand a thing here!"
From the right! — From the left! — From the right! — From the left side!
And meanwhile the beam lay waiting in the shade outside.

They argued all morning, they argued at noon, and nobody would give in,
nobody surrendered, nobody budged — not even the width of a pin.
From the right! — From the left! — From the right! — From the left side!
And meanwhile the beam lay waiting in the shade outside.

Up stood tall Reb Zalman and cried, "I've got it! It's simple and clear!
We'll saw the beam in two — one half for the right, one half for the left, my dear!
These will hold one half, and those the other — and that's how it's done!"
And everyone clapped: "What an idea! He's a genius, number one!"

Zz-zz-zz! the saw sang, and the beam was cut in two,
these grabbed one half, and those the other, with both hands, it's true.
But wait! Each half has a right side, and a left side too —
and again the study hall rang: "From the right!" "From the left!" "From the right!" "From the left!" — the whole day through.

Up stood Reb Zalman: "Again! We'll cut each half in two!"
Zz-zz-zz! — four pieces, and each had two sides, through and through.
From the right! — From the left! — From the right! — From the left side!
And meanwhile the pieces lay waiting in the shade outside.

Zz-zz-zz! Eight pieces! Zz-zz-zz! Sixteen — they sawed without a break,
and each chunk had a right and a left, while sawdust swirled like snow in a storm, flake after flake.
And everyone sneezed: "Achoo! Achoo! Achoo!"
But nobody gave up — not even because of achoo!

Zz-zz-zz, till nothing was left but teeny-tiny chips, so small,
and each tiny chip had a right and a left — just like the big ones, after all!
From the right! — From the left! — From the right! — From the left side!
And meanwhile the beam was just a heap in the shade outside.

And at last there was only a little pile of yellow sawdust on the ground,
and the greens and the oranges stood all around, not knowing what to do with what they'd found.
Gitele laughed: "Let's cut a new beam today!
One at the right end, and one at the left end — and we'll carry it together, hooray!"

They came down from the forest singing, together, greens and oranges side by side,
marching in step, and with every step their smiles grew wide.
Right! — Left! — Right! — Left! — stride after stride,
and the beam no longer lay waiting in the shade outside.

In the big study hall there's a new beam, straight and whole,
and the ceiling doesn't creak anymore — it's quiet and happy, bless its soul.
And Yokel swept up the sawdust and asked nervously, "The broom — from the right or from the left?"
And Gitele winked: "With both hands, Yokel." And everyone laughed.
